sources.entry: Family Accounting Tool - Web-based finance management tool for partners with partially shared expenses. Apache-2.0 Scala

summary.one_liner: Family Accounting Tool is a self-hosted, web-based app for tracking family transactions, calculating internal debts between partners, and checking for unexplained money loss.
summary.what_it_does: The app records every transaction a family makes, with each transaction tied to a beneficiary, a payment account (a person or the common account), and a category. It is meant to produce statistics from that data, such as monthly spending per category. It calculates what the family owes each member when one person pays for something with their own money. A cash flow overview tracks the balance of each payment method (cash, card, etc.), so the user can re-count money and spot hidden costs or losses. The README describes an endowment mechanism for transfers from individual accounts into the common account. It also mentions hidden advanced features, exchange rates and inflation correction, without details.
use_cases: calculate who owes whom between partners
monitor family shared expenses in a common account
spot hidden bank fees or missing cash
self-host a family budgeting web app
how_to_run: Download 'Binaries (compiled files) with demo configuration' from the latest release and unpack it
Configure a database in conf/application.conf (README example uses MariaDB/MySQL) and set play.http.secret.key and app.setup.defaultPassword
Run bin/server -DcreateAdminUser to create the admin user, then bin/server to start the application
Browse to the server and log in as admin / changeme
notable: Calculates internal debt between family members when one person pays for shared items
Cash flow overview with balance checks per payment method to detect unaccounted money
Special accounting category for expenses that will be reimbursed, excluded from surplus/deficit analysis
Configured via conf/accounting-config.yml with a demo configuration bundled in the release
caveats: The README says the Docker installation is discouraged for real data; installation from a release archive is recommended
Requires a separately configured database server, with MariaDB as the suggested option
Advanced features such as exchange rates and inflation correction are described as hidden and are not documented
